brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full base cells in a row at (-1,0,0), (0,0,0), (1,0,0) on level 0, locked together with joint bolts and capped open faces.
Each cell holds a bin: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0 (hex-bin-full-drain).
All three bins use the drained stem hex-bin-full-drain (full depth, drained).
Each bin filled with soil and planted: basil, mint, and flat-leaf parsley (harvest stage) via fill_and_plant, no prop warnings; check_build clear.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter in a straight row. Each full base cell carries a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain), filled with soil and planted with basil, mint, and parsley. Open faces capped and joints locked per house rules; check_build passes with meshClash clear and no issues.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three cells in a row, each with a draining herb bin — I'll check the current build and find the draining bins to lay it out.
